D.t: Deb Haaland leads by 13.6 in the forecast and wins 99% of simulations. The cushion is about 110,653 votes; a one point swing is about 4,065 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +6.3 and D +20.9. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +6.9. Your best recent poll is Research & Polling for the Albuquerque Journal at D +8.0; your worst is SurveyUSA at D +5.4. 2 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Bernalillo, a projected net 72,249 votes; Santa Fe, a projected net 44,143 votes; Doña Ana, a projected net 14,873 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Sandoval, D +6.2, 8.4% of the vote; Valencia, R +11.0, 3.5% of the vote; Cibola, D +10.9, 1.0% of the vote; Luna, R +10.7, 0.9% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Deb Haaland runs furthest behind in Sandoval, Los Alamos, Bernalillo. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 66% of voters, 58 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.29 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 64% of voters, 60 to 40, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.19 points; Voters without a degree, 60% of voters, 56 to 44, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.00 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Deb Haaland: Immigration voters 27 to 73, Small counties 48 to 52, White voters 51 to 49. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$2.8M cash against $520K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
Registered Democrats cast 53% of the 378,049 ballots in New Mexico so far, against 30% for the other party. That is 0.2 points better for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.
